text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Mubarak discusses with prime minister the general framework of government statement to parliament and development projects in southern Egypt. Ganzouri says 300 billion pounds will be spent on developing south over the next 20 years.
- Ministerial committee follows through on economic conference -- implementation in 1997 of 50 projects worth 24 billion pounds that will create 142,000 jobs.
- Egypt condemns Israeli government decision on settlements which it considers violation of international law and of peace agreements.
- President meets U.S. ambassador to Cairo -- Walker says U.S. appreciates Egypt's efforts to push forward peace process.
- Presidential adviser Baz says upon return from U.S. trip that Egypt's role in the region will never be decided by anyone else.
- Egypt and Turkey set plan to start exporting Egyptian gas to Turkey.
-- Customs council studying 10-15 percent reduction of duties on spare parts and accessories needed for electrical appliances.
- Prime Minister Ganzrouri announces start of work in Sheikh Zaid canal.
- Number of Bilharzia sufferers down by 5 percent.
- Cabinet and investment committee to issue new investment law within weeks.
- Housing minister calls for unified law and for creation of special court for violators.
